After 3 months, the bikes become the property of the Region. It repairs reusable bicycles and returns them to municipalities, CPAS, non-profit organizations, schools, etc. Currently, 15 Brussels municipalities have signed this agreement and are collaborating with the central repository for found bicycles. Description: The Department of Culture, Youth and Media wants to conduct research into the theme of integrity in youth work. Integrity is a social theme that is receiving a lot of attention. There is already a strong focus on subsidized youth work creating a safe environment for children and young people, but also focusing on learning about issues and reconnecting through a recovery-oriented approach. Furthermore, further expectations regarding integrity have been formulated in recent years Flemish Government. The Youth Decree of 23 November 2023 defines an integrity policy as a set of policy instruments at organizational level with the objectives: • the preservation and promotion of the individual physical, psychological and sexual integrity of persons; • promoting the integrity of the organization as a whole and the integrity of its youth workers. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: GENERAL MANAGEMENT SUSTAINABLE AND RAIL MOBILITY POLICY. Summary: The Organization of a Targeted Survey on the Daily Travel of Belgians Using a Dynamic Questionnaire. Description: This contract concerns the organization of a targeted survey on the daily travel of Belgians using a dynamic questionnaire. It aims more specifically to obtain data on the movements of Belgians, adults (18 years and over) and children (6 years-17 years) and who are not or no longer available from other sources, collected in the past via large-scale surveys carried out by or in collaboration with the FPS Mobility and Transport (MOBEL, BELDAM surveys and more recently MONITOR). This survey will be carried out online by a survey office with a sufficiently large panel of respondents. The FPS Mobility and Transport will analyze the data with the aim of describing mobility habits at the level of the Belgian population and also according to different general characteristics (gender, age group, region of residence, etc.). The aggregated results of the analyzes will be the subject of oral or written publications by the FPS Mobility and Transport. Category (CPV code): Survey conduction services (79311200). Two pillars are central: on the one hand an international benchmark and on the other hand a case study. The purpose of the benchmark is to gain insight into the instruments (may be broader than permits) or techniques (regulatory or not) that other representative Member States or regions use to achieve the same objectives as those of Title II of the VLAREM, namely the prevention or limitation of unacceptable nuisance and risks arising from operations, and the positive and negative elements that are experienced, such as complexity. The purpose of the case study is to investigate how unacceptable nuisance and risks for ZS can be limited by legally anchoring a Flemish ZS policy. The research should provide insights, including on the basis of a comparative legal study, into how flexible and legally certain environmental standards or conditions can be anchored, taking into account, among other things, the standstill principle. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG COMP - COMPETITION. Summary: Study on Modern Pricing and Risks of Collusion. Description: DG COMP is working on a follow-up to the comprehensive 2024 report: “Protecting competition in a changing world: Evidence on the evolution of competition in the EU during the past 25 years”. This report identified important changes over the past 25 years in the competitive environment (rising concentration, markups and profits, declining business dynamism). It also identified a number of likely structural and institutional drivers of those changes (rise of intangible investments, globalisation, regulation and M&A). The 2024 report did however not explore whether changes in management practices (strategies and tactics) may also have contributed to some of the detected trends. The present study seeks to address this gap by exploring whether the rise of modern pricing and revenue management strategies and tactics may have partly contributed to some of the observed changes in the competitive environment, inter alia by increasing the risk of collusion. <br> Doc Title: Study on modern pricing and risks of collusion <br> Contract Type: services. Tender Value: 350000. Currency: EUR. Published Date: 2025-10-20. Closing Date: 2025-11-17. Competition: ICB. Financier Name: European Commission

input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: DEPARTMENT OF WELFARE, PUBLIC HEALTH AND FAMILY. Summary: Development of Support Resources and Scripts for the Efficient Use of Resources to Prevent Tiger Mosquito-Transmitted Infectious Diseases in Flanders. Description: Since the start of national mosquito surveillance and monitoring in 2022, an increasing spread of tiger mosquitoes (Aedes albopictus) in Flanders has been reported annually. Local control keeps populations under control, but is not successful in order to completely eradicate those tiger mosquito populations, the dense buildings in Flanders make us extra vulnerable to invasion by the tiger mosquito. At the same time, we have seen an increase in outbreaks of mosquito-borne diseases worldwide in recent years. Travel to endemic areas causes an increase in the number of imported disease cases in Belgium and Flanders. Because the tiger mosquito established itself locally in Flanders, this can lead to autochthonous transmission of previously tropical diseases. This is a worrying development for which we in Flanders can better prepare. After all, the risk of local transmission of these mosquito diseases depends on future heat periods, the investment in, and efficiency of, surveillance, monitoring and control. This government contract specifically focuses on: • Developing scenarios, clear procedures and practical tools for local interventions with regard to the prevention of disease transmission by the tiger mosquito in imported cases and native cases. • Drawing up a risk mapping (both in time and space) based on scientifically supported risk factors, which reduce the risk of local dense tiger mosquitoes.... Summary: Creation Communication Tools and Concept for Sustainability Campaign for Red Meat in Flanders and Germany. Description: VLAM is developing a campaign about the sustainability initiatives of the Belgian meat sector for Flanders and Germany. The campaign is conceived as a PR campaign with a paid media component. With the PR approach, we want to highlight the sustainability of the meat sector. We aim to showcase the efforts being made within the meat sector. The tone we set in our communication is clear, honest, and trustworthy. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG COMP - COMPETITION. Summary: Study on Modern Pricing and Risks of Collusion. Description: DG COMP is working on a follow-up to the comprehensive 2024 report: “Protecting competition in a changing world: Evidence on the evolution of competition in the EU during the past 25 years”. This report identified important changes over the past 25 years in the competitive environment (rising concentration, markups and profits, declining business dynamism). It also identified a number of likely structural and institutional drivers of those changes (rise of intangible investments, globalisation, regulation and M&A). The 2024 report did however not explore whether changes in management practices (strategies and tactics) may also have contributed to some of the detected trends. The present study seeks to address this gap by exploring whether the rise of modern pricing and revenue management strategies and tactics may have partly contributed to some of the observed changes in the competitive environment, inter alia by increasing the risk of collusion. <br> Doc Title: Study on modern pricing and risks of collusion <br> Contract Type: services. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: EUROPEAN COMMISSION, DG CNECT - COMMUNICATIONS NETWORKS, CONTENT AND TECHNOLOGY. Summary: User Observations on Usage of Recommender Systems to Enable Scaling of Recommender Systems Experiments through Automated and Agentic Means. Description: Pursuant to article 27 DSA, providers of online platforms must clearly explain in their terms and conditions the main parameters used in their recommender systems, using plain and intelligible language. input: Country: Belgium. Purchaser Name: ANIMAL WELFARE DEPARTMENT. Summary: Animal Production with an Eye for Animal Welfare and Environment. Description: Animal welfare is an increasingly important theme within modern livestock farming, partly due to social concern about intensive production systems. Economic and environmental objectives, such as emission reduction and efficient use of space, are often placed above the well-being of animals. Technological Environmental measures, such as air washers in herbal, can negatively influence animal welfare. On the other hand, animal welfare measures, such as slow -growing broiler chickens, can have environmental parts. These contradictions make it clear that integrated solutions, taking into account Economic factors and use of space are needed to unite both aspects. The aim of the public contract is to give an overview of the current knowledge about the relationship between animal welfare and the environment in livestock farming. In addition, the assignment aims at the gaps in existing literature to map and prepare realistic policy recommendations. The public contract is part of the Animal Welfare policy area, "the needs of the animal" are always taken as a starting point.<br> Category (CPV code): Survey Services (79311000). Establish a detailed assessment of vegetation fires in Belgium, from historical data, in order to produce Robust descriptive statistics and an update of the National Light Starting Card. 2. Develop one or more models to characterize the potential fuel of ecosystems, by integrating biotic and abiotic data, to assess the quantity, nature and distribution in time and in the space of natural fuels. 3.
